claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-044 was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk, specifically approval-readiness failure from unresolved storage-control inconsistency, undocumented quality process, limited delivery history, and procurement's documented need for follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved.
specific_concerns: The record described in the packet appears to support follow-up or escalation more clearly than outright rejection.
The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk; the summary does not show that materiality determination directly.
A documented recommendation for follow-up before approval is not the same as a documented recommendation to reject.
Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the underlying wording, timing, and severity cannot be independently verified.
The packet correctly disclaims a proven control failure, but it still may overstate that the remaining facts are sufficient for rejection rather than further diligence.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible evidence, as summarized, is sufficient by itself to meet the reject threshold rather than only justify follow-up or escalation.
That the unresolved storage-control inconsistency was definitively material at the time of decision.
That cumulative weak indicators necessarily established approval-readiness failure under policy rather than an incomplete diligence record requiring more investigation.
evidence_requests: The exact text of BPROC-044-B through BPROC-044-E, especially any statement tying the storage-control issue to material unresolved risk.
Any formally logged materiality assessment or approval criteria showing why the unresolved items crossed the rejection threshold.
The procurement note's precise language on whether unresolved storage controls required rejection, temporary hold, or additional follow-up before decision.
Any admissible due-diligence checklist or policy mapping showing which approval condition was unsatisfied at decision time.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Do not treat quality-process gaps or questionnaire inconsistencies alone as proof of a reject-level control failure.
Do not rely on private security-review results unless formally logged.
Distinguish evidence supporting follow-up or escalation from evidence sufficient for final rejection.
Require a supportable link between the cited facts and the policy threshold for rejection.
